articles.title: Nashville Airport Could Be Renamed for Dolly Parton, Tennessee Governor Announces
articles.summary: Country music icon, actress and philanthropist Dolly Parton dedicated her life to giving back to her home state of Tennessee, and now, three days after her death, her state is ready to give back to her, renewing an earlier proposal to rename the Nashville International Airport in her honor.
body: According to the statement, Parton’s team supports the change and is “touched by the idea and open to continuing the conversation.” With her Dollywood Foundation and Imagination Library, Parton’s profound influence on Tennessee and the country is widely recognized.

The name change was first proposed last year when a petition was started in the wake of a proposal to rename the airport for President Trump. The number of signatures on the petition exploded after her death.

“Dolly’s remarkable legacy reminds us that what makes Nashville special is our ability to welcome people from every walk of life,” Doug Kreulen, president and CEO of Metropolitan Nashville Airport Authority said. “She understood that dignity, kindness and opportunity should never be defined by where you come from or your socioeconomic status.”

Nashville Mayor Freddie O’Connell expressed his support on social media, writing, “Dolly was in the process of working with us on a remarkable hotel and museum — SongTeller — that she called her love letter to Nashville. Now it’s our turn to share a love letter to Dolly — by renaming Nashville International Airport to Dolly Parton International Airport in Nashville.”

articles.title: Everything We Know About ‘Grand Theft Auto VI’
articles.summary: More than a decade after the last installment of “Grand Theft Auto” released, players are finally getting “GTA 6” on Nov. 19. Per the official description for “GTA 6” from publisher Rockstar Games, “Jason and Lucia have always known the deck is stacked against them.
body: The game is currently set to release on the PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X and S devices, meaning it won’t be available to play on older generations of the gaming consoles. There is no confirmation on when it will arrive on the PC, but previous “GTA” games have been released on consoles before expanding to PCs later.

Rockstar’s “GTA” franchise is already known for its photorealistic characters and lifelike movements, and “GTA 6” will be no different. On Aug. 27, Netflix released an extended preview of the game captured entirely on PlayStation 5.

The preview teases Jason and Lucia in scenes across the fictional Vice City, the Miami-inspired city players are familiar with. But “GTA 6” expands beyond city limits into Leonida, inspired by Florida, which is home to various distinct regions, like the Leonida Keys, Grassrivers, Port Gellhorn, Mount Kalaga and an area called Ambrosia.
Players who have allegedly seen the game say the map for “GTA 6” is significantly larger than the playable area in previous games. Rockstar has not officially confirmed this.

articles.title: Hooters Restaurant Movie in the Works — Film News in Brief
articles.summary: First the Blackberry and Hot Cheetos got the feature film treatment, and now: “Hooters: The Movie.” Based on real-life events that took place at the restaurant, the founders of Hooters are turning their business into a movie, which is already in the works, first reported by Deadline.
body: Jon Rosenbaum will direct the script written by Ed Droste, Phil Olson and Chuck Melcher. It will be independently produced by members of the original Hooters founding partners. Principal photography is scheduled to begin in November.

Brad Pitt as Cliff Booth returns for another wild ride in “The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth,” directed by David Fincher with a screenplay by Quentin Tarantino. But this time, it’s Hollywood in 1977.
The feature follow-up to “Once Upon a Time in Hollywood” will be released in Imax theaters globally for an exclusive two-week run starting Nov. 25, before debuting on Netflix on Dec. 23.

Alongside Pitt will be Elizabeth Debicki, Scott Caan, Carla Gugino, Yahya Abdul-Mateen II, Peter Weller, Matt Groove, JB Tadena, Corey Fogelmanis, and Karren Karagulian, and will be produced by Pitt and Ceán Chaffin.

articles.title: Charli XCX electrifies Reading Festival with era-spanning set
articles.summary: The British singer and Irish rock band Fontaines DC both headlined the first night of Reading for 2026.
body: Charli XCX has ushered in her next era with an electrifying headline set at Reading Festival which showcased hits from across her music career.

It marked the British singer's first UK festival performance since releasing her latest studio album - Music, Fashion, Film - which is a pivot from her culture-shaping, electronic-pop record Brat and features more of a rock edge.
But her Friday evening show highlighted the best of both, alongside fan favourite tracks from her back catalogue.

She also upped the production from her last Brat tour, with more elaborate staging, numerous costume changes, dramatic pyro and strobe lighting, and she was accompanied by a host of dancers and a live band.

articles.title: ‘I don’t care if I look good’: French heartthrob Louis Garrel on fashion, fatherhood and his radically dorky new role
articles.summary: The star has long been French cinema’s favourite tousle-haired Adonis, which makes his latest performance – as a schlubby, stay-at-home dad – all the more surprising. ‘I appreciate people laughing at me,’ he says.
body: ‘E ven though I’ve been working in film for over 20 years, I still have this desire to look beautiful on screen,” says Louis Garrel, on a video call from his bed inside a boat off the coast of Corsica. The French film star is lying on his stomach, occasionally kicking up his bare legs, ruffling his curls and running the nail of his thumb over his moustache. I think the person he sees on the laptop screen in front of him is me, but I am pretty certain he is flirting with his own reflection.

The attraction between the Paris-born 43-year-old and the camera tends to be reciprocal. Long of limb, tousled of hair and chiselled of nose, Garrel has spent a career on screen as French cinema’s favourite Adonis – the man film-makers turn to when they need an erotic wrecking ball to smash up bourgeois twosomes and turn them into quivering menages a trois.

articles.title: Gladys Knight Announces She’ll Partake in “Fewer Performances” Amid “Next Stage” of Career and Life
articles.summary: "I’ll be spending more time on projects with my husband and visiting with my grandbabies and am looking forward to this new era," the singer wrote in an Instagram post.
body: Gladys Knight has announced she’s cutting down on performances as she enters a “new era.”

Knight is currently on a solo tour and recently wrapped her time on the road for The Queens Tour alongside Chaka Khan, Patti LaBelle and Stephanie Mills. However, in her statement, Knight did not rule out all future live performances, writing, “I hope to see your smiling faces out and about on the road. God bless all of you and hope to see you soon.”

The announcement follows her July performance at the Hollywood Bowl with Smokey Robinson, which sparked some concern for the singer. In a recap of the performance, Billboard wrote that Knight “barely got through this show, and only by leaning heavily on her backup singers.”

Knight’s son, Shanga Hankerson, has shared his apprehensions about his mother’s busy life on tour. He previously told People in 2025 that her touring schedule was “detrimental” to her health, alleging that her husband, William McDowell, has been “mental[ly] and financial[ly]” abusive to Knight.

articles.title: Memo to Ridley Scott: no one needs more Alien: Covenant movies – get the franchise back to stalk’n’slash
articles.summary: News that Scott is working on a follow-up to his maligned 2017 film leaves me worried the franchise has run out of shocks. If any science-fiction saga looked beyond recovery, it was the Alien franchise.
body: And then in 2024, we got Fede Álvarez’s Alien: Romulus, in which actual xenomorphs chase actual human beings down actual corridors for the clearly defined purposes of either killing them or putting smaller xenomorphs inside them. Better still, a year later we got Noah Hawley’s Alien: Earth, which reminded us that giant, murderous space insects are in fact less awful than tech trillionaires.

It’s not the first time Scott has talked up sequels to Covenant. During the publicity run for the film, he said a follow-up was already being written and that he would start shooting within 14 months. He also suggested he could make as many as six more Alien prequels, with the series eventually leading up to the original Alien. Eight years and no prequels later, Scott announced that he had “done enough” with the franchise and merely hoped it would continue without him. Now he appears to have reverted to an earlier mode.

articles.title: Paul Heaton scores first number one album as Dolly Parton's 9 to 5 finally reaches top 40
articles.summary: Heaton's solo album tops the chart, while Parton's 1980 US hit reaches the UK top 40 at last.
body: English singer-songwriter Paul Heaton has scored his first solo UK number one album, his sixth overall.
Heaton's latest chart-topping LP - titled Jenius - follows his three with the Beautiful South and two more alongside former bandmate Jacqui Abbott.
The former Housemartins musician reached the top on Friday, in part, by shifting more vinyl copies than any other album over the past seven days.
Dolly Parton, who died earlier this week, aged 80, has three singles in the top 40, including 9 to 5, which landed at number 12 in this week's UK chart, having previously peaked at 47 in 1981.

articles.title: The Whisper Man review – Robert De Niro sleepwalks through silly Netflix potboiler
articles.summary: A father and son must team up to find a serial killer in a cheaply made and increasingly uninteresting thriller. It’s not as if Robert De Niro ’s choices have improved all that much since the nadir of the mid-2000s (last year did see him crop up in a Scott Eastwood-led actioner and The Alto Knights…
body: It’s a familiar pile of B-movie schlock – serial killers, missing children, bumps in the night, more imaginary friends – and there is some initial junky fun to be had as we wonder just where it all might be headed. I was hoping for a destination a little more deranged or vaguely surprising, the film making a silent promise that we’re hurtling toward somewhere wildly unexpected before dumping us in a ditch instead.

Like Ashcroft, De Niro is on full checked-out autopilot mode, quietly mumbling perfunctory dialogue while seemingly focused on what he’ll be having for dinner, and Scott feels uncomfortably miscast, his other hard-drinking, fiction-writing genre turn of the year proving to be considerably more effective. An actor traditionally associated with comedy, he often falls into the Steve Carell trap of confusing sitcom histrionics with dramatic hysteria and so his pain and anger at the disappearance of his son never really registers (it would also require some miraculous heavy lifting to sell some of his character’s bafflingly dumb decisions).
